articles.body: so i was looking at task manager one day and realized how much ram my computer was using. naturally, instead of closing some programs like a normal person, i decided to make my own task manager. except this one has a cat. and he hates you. introducing meowtop meowtop is a system monitor i made using python, pyqt6, and psutil. it shows your cpu, ram, and disk usage, lists running processes, and can notify you when your ram usage gets too high. but that's boring. so i added tuft. tuft is a purple cat who lives inside the app and judges your computer usage. he has different moods, animations, and a concerning number of insults. if your ram usage gets too high, he'll complain about it. if a program starts using an unreasonable amount of memory, he'll question your decisions.

articles.title: PhantomShell: the haunted terminal that whispers the fix
articles.excerpt: PhantomShell 👻 — the terminal that whispers the fix Built for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge: Week 4 — theme: Ghost in the Machine. At 2 a.m. the only thing still talking in my terminal i…
articles.body: PhantomShell 👻 — the terminal that whispers the fix Built for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge: Week 4 — theme: Ghost in the Machine . At 2 a.m. the only thing still talking in my terminal is the error message. gti: command not found — five words, no context, no apology, no hint about what it wanted. It says what went wrong and stays completely silent about what should have happened. It is, in the most literal sense available to me, a ghost: a voice from a dead process, speaking a language of exit codes and stack traces, saying nothing that matters. Every shell tool I have used treats that voice as raw material. They parse it, they grep it, they open a ticket with it. I built something that listens to it instead. PhantomShell is a small ghost that lives in your shell hook.
articles.author: Md Faijal Eaqbal

articles.title: Telegram Inline Bots: Avatar Template Picker with aiogram 3
articles.excerpt: The Problem: Telegram Video Avatars Are Picky Setting a video avatar in Telegram sounds simple until you try it on an iPhone. Telegram silently rejects HEVC (H.265) files, which is what every modern i…
articles.body: The Problem: Telegram Video Avatars Are Picky Setting a video avatar in Telegram sounds simple until you try it on an iPhone. Telegram silently rejects HEVC (H.265) files, which is what every modern iOS device records by default. No error message. Just nothing happens. Users think the bot is broken. The actual Telegram spec for video avatars: codec H.264, resolution 800x800 (square), max 10 seconds, max 2MB, no audio. Getting all five constraints right simultaneously is what I built @liveavabot for. But once you have a working converter, the next question is: how do users pick templates without leaving their current chat? That's where inline mode comes in. Why Inline Mode Is the Right UX Most bots ignore inline_query .

articles.title: Subscriber Shipment Fan-Out: 4 Recovery Boundaries for Rate-Limited Queue Consumption
articles.excerpt: The expensive part of a shipment-update fan-out is rarely the queue write. It is the work that remains retained while a downstream provider says “slow down,” plus the duplicate sends and manual invest…
articles.body: The expensive part of a shipment-update fan-out is rarely the queue write. It is the work that remains retained while a downstream provider says “slow down,” plus the duplicate sends and manual investigation created by a poor recovery path. For a media SaaS application notifying 80,000 subscribers about a physical shipment, I would choose a queue by how precisely it lets workers stop, retry, quarantine, and resume—not by its peak publish rate. Short answer: use a queue with an explicit visibility or acknowledgment boundary, durable delayed retry behavior, and a dead-letter path you can inspect. Put the dynamic limiter in the consumer layer, keyed by the destination or provider policy.

articles.body: IMA appraisal covers files, not the whole trust path The Linux Integrity Measurement Architecture can collect hashes for executed and accessed files and can support appraisal against trusted signatures or stored hashes. That control is useful for detecting or blocking a modified system binary. It is not a complete statement that the machine is trustworthy. IMA measurement records runtime evidence. Appraisal makes a policy decision using security metadata, trust anchors, and a configured policy. The kernel documentation describes IMA templates, file signatures, and EVM interactions. A signature may be based on a file digest or an EVM portable signature, and the kernel needs a trusted key and keyring path before it can make the expected decision.

articles.title: Artemis II commander Reid Wiseman named deputy director for NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory
articles.excerpt: The leader of NASA's first mission around the moon in half a century is the last to announce what's next for him after retiring from active astronaut duty.
articles.body: The leader of NASA's first mission around the moon in half a century is the last to announce what's next for him after retiring from active astronaut duty. All four astronauts of the Artemis II mission, which flew around the moon in April, have hung up their spacesuits and moved on to greener pastures. NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), managed by Caltech, announced yesterday that former NASA astronaut Reid Wiseman will step into the role of Caltech associate vice president and deputy director of JPL, beginning Nov. 30. "Reid has spent his career at the edge of what is possible, and he has the technical judgment, operational experience, and leadership to help push that edge farther," NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said in a JPL press release .

articles.title: Astronauts deploy solar array on 100th US spacewalk by International Space Station crew members
articles.excerpt: NASA astronaut Anil Menon and Joshua Kutryk of the Canadian Space Agency deployed a new solar array on Thursday (Oct. 29) during a seven-hour spacewalk outside the International Space Station.
articles.body: Two astronauts successfully installed and deployed the second-to-last upgraded solar array for the International Space Station (ISS) during the 100th U.S. spacewalk from the orbiting outpost. Anil Menon of NASA and Joshua Kutryk of the Canadian Space Agency (CSA), both ISS Expedition 75 crewmates, completed the 7-hour-and-11-minute extravehicular activity (EVA) at 3:08 p.m. EDT (1908 GMT) on Thursday (Oct. 29). The spacewalk began and ended inside the U.S. Quest airlock, with both astronauts wearing NASA's extravehicular mobility unit (EMU) spacesuits. It was the first spacewalk by a Canadian astronaut since April 2019, when David Saint-Jacques ventured into the void with NASA's Anne McClain.

articles.excerpt: Final Fantasy Resonance is everything Square Enix's RPG series has struggled to achieve ove the last decade, and it should guide the series' future
articles.body: I had few expectations going into Final Fantasy Resonance , the premium game based on Square Enix's mobile gacha Brave Exvius . Those expectations lowered in the first 10 hours, thanks to its frankly atrocious writing. But after clearing most of the story and approaching the endgame, I find I've changed stances entirely. Resonance is everything Final Fantasy has struggled to achieve over the better part of two decades — confident, innovative, engaging, and, most importantly, completely and unashamedly itself. It's the blueprint Square Enix needs to follow for the series' future.
articles.author: Josh Broadwell

articles.title: 'Crystal Lake' is great, but nothing tops the space horror shenanigans of 'Jason X'
articles.excerpt: The Voorhees legend continues in Crystal Lake, but Jason X remains the Citizen Kane of this franchise.
articles.body: Peacock's "Crystal Lake" takes the story of the Voorhees family back to the beginning. It's a full-circle moment revisiting Pamela Voorhees (Linda Cardellini), who's the real star of 1980's "Friday the 13th" and the catalyst for all the murder and mayhem. While it's a welcome shake-up to the timeline of the horror franchise, nothing tops the originality of the slasher-in-space spectacle known as "Jason X". It was 2001, and the "Friday the 13th" franchise had hit a bit of a snag. Audiences had seen Jason Voorhees go everywhere from Crystal Lake to Manhattan and Hell, but where else could this hockey-masked killer go? Screenwriter Todd Farmer had the answer: space . "Jason X" says the quiet part out loud: Jason (Kane Hodder) can't die.

articles.excerpt: When a rose-colored meteorite was found in the Sahara Desert in 2022, no one knew how old it was or where it came from. Not until NASA-funded scientists age-dated its minerals did they realize the nea…
articles.body: 5 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) Called Teghaza 001, this rose-colored rock is one of the most ancient Martian meteorites ever found on Earth. Credit: © Darryl Pitt / Maine Mineral & Gem Museum When a rose-colored meteorite was found in the Sahara Desert in 2022, no one knew how old it was or where it came from. Not until NASA-funded scientists age-dated its minerals did they realize the nearly 2-pound (800-gram) rock was a piece of Mars that formed more than 4.1 billion years ago, making it one of the oldest Martian meteorites ever found. Named Teghaza 001 after the salt plain in Mali where it was discovered, the meteorite is one of roughly 435 from the Red Planet.

articles.title: Cosmic graveyard of zombie planets offers a grisly warning about our own solar system's fate
articles.excerpt: Two zombie exoplanets that rose from the grave to shuffle through the gory remains of their fellow planets may just agree with these immortal words from horror maestro Stephen King.
articles.body: "Sometimes dead is better." Who can forget the immortal words of Jud Crandall, delivered by the incomparable Fred Gwynne in the 1989 film adaptation of Stephen King's Pet Sematary? Turns out Crandall could have been talking about somewhere just as otherworldly as the cursed Chumash burial ground at the heart of one of King's most terrifying works of fiction. That's because astronomers have discovered two husks of two zombie planets shuffling through the gory remains of what was once their planetary neighbors around a long-deceased star, or white dwarf. The shattered planets were revealed by a clear gap in the debris around the white dwarf J1328−1450, located around 1,600 light-years away from Earth.
